enriquez2017.src: Enriquez et al. 2017, ApJ 849, 104, abstract: 'none of the observed systems host high-duty-cycle radio transmitters ... with an Equivalent Isotropic Radiated Power of ~10^13 W ... fewer than ~0.1% of the stellar systems within 50 pc'.

margot2023.src: Margot et al. 2023, AJ 166, 206, sec. 6: 'fewer than 6.6% of the 331,312 stars within 100 pc host a transmitter that is detectable in our survey (EIRP > 1.35 x 10^13 W) ... For stars located within 20,000 ly, ... (EIRP > 5.08 x 10^16 W)'.  20,000 ly = 6135 pc.  NOTE: the superseded v3.24 figure plotted the near point at 1.0e13 W; the published value is 1.35e13 W and is used here.

mason2024.src: Mason et al. 2024, MNRAS 536, 2127, sec. 4: 'the smallest minimum detectable power ... is 6.91 x 10^17 W for the closest target star (Gaia DR3 4154920820659128192)'; that star's distance in their Table 2 is 1.010 kpc.

price2020.src: Price et al. 2020, AJ 159, 86, abstract: 'we can put an upper limit on the power of potential radio transmitters at these frequencies at 2x10^12 W, and 9x10^12 W for GBT and Parkes respectively'.  These are deepest per-target limits, not a single sample distance, so they are drawn as left-edge ticks rather than as points in distance.
